recorded_response.assistant_text: Imagine it's six months from now and Accelerate Acquisition didn't get you to £20k MRR. What went wrong? Here are the most likely failure modes based on your model's structure. New subscriber acquisition stalls. This is the single biggest risk. The model shows acquisition rate driving 100% of the outcome sensitivity. If your acquisition channel hits a ceiling, gets more expensive, or faces increased competition, the whole strategy unravels. What's your current acquisition channel, and how confident are you it can scale? Churn erodes the gains. Bringing in new subscribers only works if you keep them. If price sensitivity is higher than assumed, or if the product doesn't retain at scale, net subscriber growth could disappoint even with strong acquisition numbers. The £20k target requires more subscribers than the timeline allows. At £49/month, you need roughly 409 subscribers to hit £20k MRR. If you're starting from a low base, the maths may simply not work within six months regardless of the acquisition strategy.
